about.title: Rancho Palos Verdes Medical Malpractice Claims
about.longDescription: Rancho Palos Verdes residents often travel to nearby South Bay hospitals and clinics for care, and most of the time that care goes as expected. But when a diagnosis is missed, a surgery goes wrong, or medication is mishandled, the effects can follow someone for years. California treats these cases differently than a typical injury claim — there are shorter windows to act, a required expert review, and a formal notice step before a lawsuit can even be filed. Our team handles medical malpractice matters and can explain, in plain terms, whether a bad outcome might actually be a legal claim. The conversation costs nothing, and there's no obligation to move forward.

whyChoose.title: Why Timing and Detail Matter in These Cases

items.title: MICRA's Clock Starts Fast
items.desc: California generally gives you one year from when you discover the harm, and no more than three years from the injury itself, to bring a claim. Waiting to sort out what happened can cost you the right to act at all.

items.title: A 90-Day Notice Comes First
items.desc: Before a malpractice lawsuit can be filed in California, the provider must typically receive 90 days' written notice. Our team familiar with this step can help make sure it's handled correctly and on time.

items.title: Expert Review Is Almost Always Required
items.desc: California law generally requires a qualified medical expert to support a malpractice claim — a bad result by itself isn't enough. We can help arrange that kind of review before deciding how to proceed.

items.question: Is every bad medical outcome considered malpractice?
items.answer: No. California law is clear that a poor result alone doesn't prove negligence — medicine involves risk even when providers act reasonably. We would need to look at whether the care fell below the accepted standard, which usually requires a medical expert's opinion.

items.question: I live in Rancho Palos Verdes but was treated at a hospital in another city — does that matter?
items.answer: Not for whether you can pursue a claim. What matters is where the treatment happened and where the provider is licensed, not your home address. Our team can sort out the right venue and requirements based on the facts of your case.

items.question: How long do I actually have to bring a claim in California?
items.answer: Generally, it's one year from when you discovered (or reasonably should have discovered) the injury, but never more than three years from the date it occurred, with some exceptions. Because there's also a 90-day pre-suit notice requirement, it's worth talking to someone sooner rather than later.

items.question: Is there a cost to speak with you?
items.answer: No. Our initial consultation is free, and we work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless you recover something. There's no upfront cost or obligation to speak with us.
